title: The Passage of the Sepik Basin
premise: Wren Blackwood, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Voss brothers—cheerful lenders who collect in blood—flees to Papua New Guinea chasing a rumor: a tidal cave in the Sepik Basin that floods once a season and hides a fortune in pre-war artifacts. But the cave's guardian, an old riverwoman named Ila, recognizes Wren as the daughter she gave up decades ago, and the Voss brothers' enforcer arrives to claim both Wren and the treasure. To survive, Wren must cross the Finisterre Range ahead of the snows and outrun the monsoon carrying her debt, her mother, and the man who loves her—river guide Tomas Kerebu—toward a final reckoning at the coast, where she trades the treasure for her freedom and chooses, at last, to be someone rather than no one.
about_author: Astrid Vane is the pen name of a former field researcher who spent three years along the Sepik River documenting oral histories before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels from a houseboat that has never once stayed where she parked it.

chapters.title: The Debt of Optimists
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In Cairns, the Voss brothers give her ninety days to repay a crushing loan or work it off 'their way.' She signs on to a salvage expedition to New Guinea as cover. Emotional beat: cornered desperation masked by bravado.

chapters.title: Salt and Rumor
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A drunken pearl diver tells her of a cave near the Sepik mouth that opens only at king tides, filled with Japanese war caches and older things. Wren sees her way out. Beat: reckless hope kindling.

chapters.title: The River That Forgets Nothing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She reaches the Sepik Basin and hires Tomas Kerebu, a guide who reads water like scripture and distrusts her instantly. Beat: friction between two people who need each other.

chapters.title: Ila of the Reed Houses
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He brings Wren to his aunt Ila, the basin's oldest spirit-keeper, who goes still at the sight of Wren's eyes. Beat: unease; something is recognized before anyone says it aloud.

chapters.title: King Tide
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The tide drops and the sea-cave yawns open. Inside: crates, bones, and a carved stone that hums with significance Ila will later demand back. Beat: awe curdling into greed she doesn't want to admit.

chapters.title: What the Cave Charged
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. Ila reveals fragments: a foreign woman, forty years ago, a baby left with the river people. Wren refuses to believe. Beat: denial as armor.

chapters.title: A Boat on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A launch flying no flag enters the delta—the Voss enforcer, Marek, has tracked Wren. Tomas warns her; she lies about how much trouble she's in. Beat: trust cracking under the weight of secrets.

chapters.title: Blood in the Sago
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Marek's men raid the village seeking the stone. Ila is hurt protecting it. Wren realizes her debt followed her here and now has a body count. Beat: guilt as ignition.

chapters.title: The Choice of Rivers
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas offers to take Wren overland to Madang ahead of the monsoon—if she surrenders the stone to Ila. She can't let go of her only leverage. Beat: love against duty, first stated plainly.

chapters.title: Leaving the Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They abandon the boat and begin the ascent into the foothills, pursued. First night in the rainforest: leeches, fever, Tomas's quiet competence. Beat: humility beginning.

chapters.title: Ila's Truth
chapters.summary: Ila's POV, interlude. Ila recounts the full story of Wren's mother—a cartographer who fled the Voss family's fathers—and why the stone must never be sold. Beat: grief across generations.

chapters.title: The Finisterre Wall
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The range rears up; porters desert; snows are weeks early. Wren's storm-chaser instincts become survival skills. Beat: competence earned, self-worth stirring.

chapters.title: Marek's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek catches them at a mission station and offers Wren a deal: the stone for her debt, or he takes Tomas instead. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: What Wren Won't Pay
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She refuses; they fight free of the station but Tomas takes a bullet graze. Fevered, he asks why she matters more than money. She has no answer yet. Beat: love confessed sideways.

chapters.title: Above the Cloud Line
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The climb through cloud forest; Tomas weakens; Wren carries him partway. She stops being invisible to herself. Beat: identity forged in effort.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The storm hits early—her own specialty turned enemy. Landslides close the pass; they shelter in a limestone sinkhole with the stone between them. Beat: nature indifferent to human stakes.

chapters.title: The Descent to Madang
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. They descend the wet side through flooded ravines, racing the rising rivers. Marek's men shadow them, also fighting the weather. Beat: pursuit and endurance braided together.

chapters.title: Reckoning at the Coast
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At Madang's harbor, cornered, Wren offers Marek the stone—but Ila arrives by coastal trader and invokes a customary claim that makes its sale taboo to every local broker. Marek's leverage collapses. Beat: community as weapon.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Stripped of the stone, Marek demands payment in person. Wren gives him her salvage rights, her gear, and her name on the expedition ledger—everything but Tomas and the truth. Beat: costly, clean surrender.

chapters.title: Stone Returned
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. Ila returns the stone to the cave at the next tide, and formally names Wren as kin before the village. Wren weeps for the mother she never knew. Beat: belonging after exile.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Instead of fleeing, Wren stays through the monsoon, working the river with Tomas and charting safe passages from her storm knowledge. Beat: love chosen freely, not as escape.

chapters.title: The Passage
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, closing. Dry season comes; a letter from the Voss brothers arrives—debt closed, interest waived, a warning wrapped in courtesy. Wren burns it on the beach and walks back upriver. Beat: resolution; the wilderness forgives nothing, but she has finally paid herself.
